title: React skill test
summary: A timed practice assessment: multiple-choice questions on React 19, hooks, testing and TypeScript, plus two short coding tasks.

topics.title: Custom hooks and the rules of hooks

questions.prompt: What does this render when `count` is 0?
questions.explain: `count && …` evaluates to `0` when `count` is 0, and React renders numbers. Use `count > 0 && …` or a ternary.

questions.prompt: What happens with this component?
choices: It does not compile: adjacent JSX elements must be wrapped
questions.explain: A component returns one JSX expression. Wrap siblings in a fragment (`<>…</>`) or another element.

questions.prompt: What does `<card />` render here?
choices: A compile error about the name
questions.explain: Lowercase JSX tags are treated as built-in HTML elements. Component names must start with a capital letter.

questions.prompt:
Which of these values renders visible text inside `
{value}
`?
questions.explain: `true`, `false`, `null` and `undefined` render nothing. Numbers, including 0, render as text.

questions.prompt: What happens when this renders?
choices: React throws "Objects are not valid as a React child"
questions.explain: Plain objects are not valid React children. Render a field such as `{user.name}` instead.

questions.prompt: After one click, what does the button show?
questions.explain: Each call uses the `count` from this render's snapshot (0), so all three set it to 1. Use `setCount(c => c + 1)` to queue updates.

questions.prompt: After one click, what does the button show?
questions.explain: Updater functions are queued and each receives the latest pending state, so the count goes 0 → 1 → 2 → 3.

questions.prompt: What does the first click log?
questions.explain: Setting state does not change the variable in the running handler; it schedules a new render. The handler still sees the snapshot value 0.

questions.prompt: Clicking "Add" does not update the list. Why?
choices: The same array is mutated and passed back, so React sees no change
Arrays cannot be stored in state
questions.explain: React compares the new state with `Object.is`. Mutating and passing the same array can skip the re-render. Create a new array: `setItems([...items, item])`.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between these two lines?
choices: The first calls createRows() on every render; the second only on the first render
The second calls createRows() on every render
The second stores the function itself in state
questions.explain: Passing a function makes it an initialiser that React calls only once. `useState(createRows())` evaluates the call on every render and ignores the result after the first.

questions.prompt: What happens when the user types into this input?
choices: Nothing changes: the input is read-only because value is fixed and there is no onChange
questions.explain: A `value` without `onChange` makes a controlled input that cannot change. React warns; add `onChange`, use `readOnly`, or use `defaultValue`.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with this button?
choices: remove(id) runs during every render instead of on click
Arrow functions are not allowed in JSX
questions.explain: `onClick={remove(id)}` calls the function while rendering and passes its result. Pass a function: `onClick={() => remove(id)}`.

questions.prompt: Which prop sets the initial value of an uncontrolled text input?
questions.explain: `defaultValue` (and `defaultChecked`) set the initial value and leave later changes to the DOM.

questions.prompt: This form reloads the page when submitted. What is the usual fix?
questions.explain: The browser's default submit navigates. Call `event.preventDefault()` in an `onSubmit` handler (React 19 function actions also prevent it for you).

questions.prompt: What does clicking the button log?
questions.explain: React events bubble like DOM events: the button handler runs first, then the parent's. Call `e.stopPropagation()` to stop it.

questions.prompt: Why is `key={index}` risky for a list whose items can be inserted or reordered?
choices: State and DOM can stay attached to the wrong item when positions change
questions.explain: React matches items by key. When positions shift, an index key points at a different item, so inputs and state can end up on the wrong row. Use a stable id.

questions.prompt: Keys must be unique…
choices: among siblings in the same list
per render only, and may change each render
questions.explain: Keys only need to be unique among siblings. They should also be stable between renders.

questions.prompt: What happens to `<Profile>` state when `userId` changes?
choices: It is reset, because a new key mounts a new instance
questions.explain: Changing `key` tells React it is a different component, so it unmounts the old one and mounts a fresh one with new state.

questions.prompt: What does `Row` read from `props.key`?
questions.explain: `key` is used by React and is not passed to the component. Pass the value under another prop name if the child needs it.

questions.prompt: In development with StrictMode, what does mounting this component log?
questions.explain: In development StrictMode runs an extra setup + cleanup cycle on mount to reveal missing cleanups. Production logs "connect" once.

questions.prompt: When does an effect's cleanup function run?
choices: Before the effect runs again with changed dependencies, and on unmount
questions.explain: React runs cleanup with the old values before re-running the effect, and once more when the component unmounts.

questions.prompt: What does the screen show after three clicks?
questions.code:
const clicks = useRef(0)
return <button onClick={() => { clicks.current++ }}>Clicks: {clicks.current}</button>
questions.explain: Changing `ref.current` does not trigger a re-render, so the screen keeps showing the value from the last render. Use state for values you display.

questions.prompt: What does this log on the first render?
questions.explain: React sets DOM refs after it commits the DOM. During the first render `ref.current` is still the initial value, `null`. Read refs in effects or handlers.

questions.prompt: Which pattern stops an older response from overwriting a newer one?
choices: Add the response to the dependency array
Set an ignore flag in the effect cleanup and skip setState when it is set
questions.explain: When dependencies change, cleanup runs for the old effect. Setting `ignore = true` there means the old request's result is dropped.

questions.prompt: Why not write `useEffect(async () => { … })`?
choices: async functions are not allowed in components
It returns a promise, but React expects the effect to return a cleanup function or nothing
await is not supported in effects
questions.explain: An async function always returns a promise. Define an async function inside the effect and call it instead.

questions.prompt: The cleanup calls `controller.abort()` while a fetch is pending. What happens to the fetch?
choices: It rejects with an AbortError, which you should ignore
It keeps running and resolves normally
questions.explain: Aborting makes the fetch promise reject with a DOMException named "AbortError". Catch it and skip it so it is not shown as a real error.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to show `fullName` from `first` and `last` state?
choices: Store fullName in state and update it in an effect
Compute it during render: const fullName = first + " " + last
questions.explain: Values you can compute from props or state should be computed during render. An effect adds an extra render and can get out of sync.

questions.prompt: What does `useContext(ThemeContext)` return in a component with no provider above it?
choices: The default value passed to createContext
questions.explain: Without a matching provider above, `useContext` returns the default value given to `createContext`.

questions.prompt: A component wrapped in `memo` reads a context with `useContext`. The context value changes. Does it re-render?
choices: Yes, context changes re-render consumers even inside memo
Only if its props changed too
questions.explain: `memo` only skips re-renders caused by the parent with equal props. A changed context value always re-renders the components that read it.

questions.prompt: Why might every consumer re-render whenever `App` re-renders?
choices: The value is a new object on every render
questions.explain: An object literal is a new value each render, so consumers see a change. Wrap it in `useMemo` (and functions in `useCallback`).

questions.prompt: Dispatching "add" does not update the screen. Why?
choices: The reducer mutates and returns the same state object
questions.explain: Reducers must be pure and return new objects. Returning the same reference lets React skip the update. Return `{ ...state, items: [...state.items, action.item] }`.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with this code?
choices: Hooks must be called in the same order every render, so they cannot be called conditionally
Hooks must be called inside effects
questions.explain: React matches hook calls by order. A conditional hook changes the order between renders. Call hooks at the top level and put the condition inside.

questions.prompt: Two components each call `useCounter()`. What do they share?
choices: Only the logic; each call has its own state
Nothing, custom hooks cannot use state
questions.explain: Custom hooks reuse stateful logic, not state. Each call gets its own independent state. Share state with context or by lifting it up.

questions.prompt: Why should a custom hook name start with "use"?
choices: React will not run it otherwise
It lets React and the linter know the function calls hooks, so the rules of hooks can be checked
It is only a style preference with no effect
questions.explain: The `use` prefix tells readers and the hooks linter that the function calls hooks, so the rules of hooks are enforced inside and around it.

questions.prompt: Where may you call `useState`?
choices: At the top level of a component or custom hook
questions.explain: Hooks may only be called at the top level of function components and custom hooks, never in handlers, loops, conditions or effects.

questions.prompt: `Row` is wrapped in `memo`. Why does it still re-render whenever the parent does?
choices: memo does not work with function components
onSelect is a new function on every render, so the props are not equal
questions.explain: `memo` compares props with `Object.is`. A new arrow function each render is a different value. Wrap it in `useCallback`.

questions.prompt: `useCallback(fn, deps)` is equivalent to…
questions.explain: `useCallback` caches the function itself. `useMemo` caches the result of calling its function, so you wrap `fn` in another function.

questions.prompt: By default, when a parent re-renders, which children re-render?
questions.explain: Re-rendering a component re-renders everything it renders, unless a child is memoised and its props are equal.

questions.prompt: `Panel`'s own `open` state changes. Does `<Chart />` re-render?
choices: No: the Chart element was created by App and passed as children, so it is the same element
questions.explain: Elements passed as `children` were created by the parent that rendered them. When only `Panel` re-renders, `children` is the same element, so React skips it.

questions.prompt: What does `useActionState(action, initialState)` return?
questions.explain: It returns the current state, a wrapped action to pass to `<form action>` or call in a transition, and a pending flag.

questions.prompt: When does a `useOptimistic` value go back to the real state?
choices: When the action or transition that set it finishes
questions.explain: The optimistic value is shown while the async action is pending, then React shows the real state again, whether the action succeeded or failed.

questions.prompt: Which statement about `use(promise)` is true?
choices: It must be called at the top level, like other hooks
It can be called inside conditions and loops, and suspends until the promise resolves
It only works in class components
It creates the promise for you
questions.explain: `use` is an API that can be called conditionally. Pass a cached or parent-created promise; a promise created during render would be recreated each time.

questions.prompt: In React 19, how does a function component receive a `ref` from its parent?
choices: As a regular prop named ref
questions.explain: React 19 passes `ref` as a normal prop to function components. `forwardRef` still works but is no longer needed.

questions.prompt: What does `save` receive when this form is submitted?
choices: The input values as an object
questions.explain: When `action` is a function, React calls it with the form's `FormData`. After it succeeds, React resets uncontrolled fields.

questions.prompt: How do you write an error boundary today?
choices: As a class component with static getDerivedStateFromError and/or componentDidCatch
questions.explain: React has no hook for error boundaries. Write a class (or use a small library that wraps one).

questions.prompt: Which error does an error boundary catch?
choices: An error thrown in an onClick handler
An error thrown in a setTimeout callback
An error thrown while a child renders
A rejected fetch in an event handler
questions.explain: Boundaries catch errors during rendering, in lifecycle methods and effects of the tree below. Errors in event handlers and async callbacks need try/catch.

questions.prompt: What goes wrong when `lazy()` is called inside a component body?
choices: It creates a new component type every render, so its state resets
questions.explain: Declare lazy components at the top level of a module. Calling `lazy` during render returns a new type each time, which remounts the subtree.

questions.prompt: Already-visible content suspends during an update wrapped in `startTransition`. What does the user see?
choices: The previous content until the new content is ready
questions.explain: Transitions are non-urgent, so React keeps already-revealed content on screen instead of replacing it with a fallback.

questions.prompt: Which query should you use to assert that an element is NOT on screen?
questions.explain: `queryBy*` returns `null` when nothing matches. `getBy*` throws, and `findBy*` waits and then rejects.

questions.prompt: A heading appears after a mocked fetch resolves. Which query fits best?
questions.explain: `findBy*` returns a promise that retries until the element appears or the timeout passes.

questions.prompt: Which query does Testing Library recommend first?
questions.explain: Role queries (with an accessible name) match how users and assistive tech find elements. Test ids are a last resort.

questions.prompt: Why prefer `userEvent` over `fireEvent` for typing?
choices: It simulates the full interaction (focus, key events, input) like a real user
questions.explain: `fireEvent` dispatches one event. `userEvent` fires the sequence a browser would, so tests catch more real bugs.

questions.prompt: Which type accepts anything React can render as `children`?
questions.explain: `ReactNode` covers elements, strings, numbers, fragments, arrays, null and so on. `JSX.Element` only allows a single element.

questions.prompt: What is the type of `e` in an input's onChange handler?
questions.explain: React passes synthetic events. `ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>` gives `e.target.value` the right type.

questions.prompt: Why write `useState<User | null>(null)`?
choices: It is required for all state
Otherwise the type is inferred from null and you cannot set a User later
questions.explain: TypeScript infers state from the initial value. With only `null`, the type would be `null`, so give the generic explicitly.

questions.prompt: What is the type of `inputRef.current`?
questions.explain: A DOM ref starts as `null` and is `null` again after unmount, so the type includes `null`.

questions.prompt:
What is the main problem with `
Save
`?
choices: It is not focusable or keyboard-operable and has no button role
questions.explain: Use a real `<button>`: it is focusable, works with Enter and Space, and is announced as a button.

questions.prompt: How do you link a `<label>` to an input by id in JSX?
questions.explain: `for` is a reserved word in JavaScript, so JSX uses `htmlFor`. You can also wrap the input inside the label.

questions.prompt: How do you make "Saved!" get announced by screen readers when it appears?
choices: Render it in an element with role="status" (a polite live region) that is already on the page
questions.explain: Live regions announce changes to their content. Keep the region mounted and change its text.

questions.prompt: What `alt` should a purely decorative image have?
questions.explain: An empty `alt` tells assistive tech to skip the image. A missing `alt` can make screen readers read the file name.
